title: How doctors find out what is wrong
examples: What is the difference between a symptom and a sign?
Can a doctor tell what is wrong just by looking at me?
What kind of tests do doctors use for bones?

explain.say: First, a doctor listens to your symptoms. Symptoms are things you feel that tell a doctor something is wrong.

draw.text: How doctors find out what is wrong

explain.say: Next, the doctor performs an examination. This means they check different parts of your body carefully.
Then, doctors might order tests. These tests help them see what is happening inside your body.
After gathering all this information, the doctor makes a diagnosis. A diagnosis is the name of the illness they think you have.
For example, if you have a sore throat and your test shows high bacteria, the diagnosis might be strep throat.

items: Sore throat | High bacteria | Strep throat

explain.say: In real life, if you fall and cannot move your arm, your symptoms are pain and inability to move. The doctor will examine it, maybe take an X-ray test, and then give a diagnosis like a fracture.

faq.q: What is the difference between a symptom and a sign?
faq.a: A symptom is something you feel, like pain. A sign is something a doctor can observe, like a rash.
asks: Can I tell the difference between the two?

faq.q: How does a doctor know if a test is accurate?
faq.a: Doctors compare test results with known conditions and use different types of tests to be sure.
asks: Are all medical tests 100 percent correct?

faq.q: Is a diagnosis the same as a cure?
faq.a: No, a diagnosis only names the problem. A cure is the treatment that makes you well again.
asks: Does diagnosis mean I am already better?

faq.q: What if the doctor cannot find a diagnosis?
faq.a: Sometimes doctors need more time or more specialized tests to figure out what is happening.
asks: Do they ever give up trying to diagnose?

faq.q: Do I need to tell the doctor everything, even if it seems small?
faq.a: Yes, telling them everything helps them connect the small things to the big picture of your health.
asks: Is it okay to forget to tell them something?

facts: Symptoms are subjective feelings reported by the patient.
An examination involves physical checks like listening or looking.
Tests can include blood samples, X-rays, or swabs.
A diagnosis is a professional conclusion about a health condition.

quiz.say: You feel dizzy and your doctor checks your reflexes. What are the dizziness and the reflex check?
quiz.why: Dizziness is something you experience and report, which is a symptom.

wrong.1: A sign is something the doctor observes, but dizziness is felt by you.
wrong.2: A test is a procedure, like checking reflexes, not the feeling itself.
wrong.3: A diagnosis is the name given after checking symptoms and signs.

quiz.say: A doctor orders a blood test to check for infection. Which step is this?
quiz.why: Ordering a blood test is an active step taken by the doctor to gather evidence.

wrong.1: Symptoms are what the patient tells the doctor, not what the doctor orders.
wrong.2: Examination is physical checking, like listening to your heart, not taking a sample.
wrong.3: Diagnosis happens last, after all the evidence from tests is gathered.

quiz.say: If a doctor confirms you have a bacterial infection after checking your throat, what has been established?
quiz.why: The final name given to the illness after all checks is the diagnosis.

wrong.0: A test is the tool used to find out, not the final conclusion itself.
wrong.2: A symptom is just what you feel, not the confirmed name of the illness.
wrong.3: Examination is the action of checking, not the name of the problem found.
